questions.passage: But when we actually interact with a stranger, we tend to enjoy it far more than we think. In other words, we tend to underestimate how enjoyable doing something unfamiliar, like talking to a stranger, is. Social psychologists Nick Epley and Juliana Schroeder tested how much people enjoy talking to strangers in a clever field experiment on a commuter train. Their research assistants approached 118 commuters at the Homewood Metra station, one of the first stations on the express line to the Millennium Station in downtown Chicago.
questions.prompt: What mismatch motivates the commuter experiment?
options: Commuters always predict exactly what they experience.
People expect greater enjoyment than any stranger can provide.
People may enjoy unfamiliar interaction more than they anticipate.
All travellers dislike the same stations.
questions.promptZh: 什么不一致促成通勤实验？
optionsZh: 预测总与体验精确相同。
总高估陌生人能提供的快乐。
可能比预期更享受陌生互动。
所有旅客都讨厌相同车站。
analyses: A underestimate 明说预测有偏差。
B 方向反转，原文是低估。
C actual...far more than we think 概括主题。
D 地点是实验招募背景，非车站喜好比较。118 是接触的通勤者数，不是后续回收数。

evidence.quote: we tend to underestimate how enjoyable doing something unfamiliar, like talking to a stranger, is.

vocabulary.context: 对陌生互动愉悦程度的预测偏低
vocabulary.example: We sometimes underestimate how enjoyable a new conversation will be.

questions.translation: 但实际与陌生人互动时，我们往往比想象中享受得多。也就是说，我们倾向低估做陌生事情的乐趣，例如与陌生人聊天。社会心理学家 Nick Epley 和 Juliana Schroeder 在通勤列车做实地实验，检验这种乐趣。研究助理在 Homewood Metra 站接触 118 名通勤者；该站是通向 Chicago 市中心 Millennium 站快线前几站之一。

questions.passage: We are clearly mistaken to think that not making any changes to our commute and keeping to ourselves would be better than talking to a fellow commuter. We think sticking to a routine commute is better than making a new social connection: a clear familiarity bias. We settle on a job candidate or potential mate before exploring enough. We need to overcome this familiarity bias in order to explore the new and unknown.
questions.prompt: What action does the author advocate after discussing the commute findings?
options: Always choose the first candidate without exploration.
Keep every social routine unchanged.
Overcome familiarity bias to explore unfamiliar possibilities.
Treat every commute as a guaranteed benefit.

保持每个社交常规不变。
克服熟悉偏误，探索陌生可能。
把每次通勤当保证获益。
analyses: A before exploring enough 是被批评的倾向。
B 当前鼓励新联系。
C 最后一句直接表明主张。
D 没有每次保证，作者把结果延伸至候选与择偶，是应用论证而非这些领域新实验。

evidence.quote: We need to overcome this familiarity bias in order to explore the new and unknown.

vocabulary.context: 指减少偏误对探索的限制

questions.passage: Steve Jobs didn’t suffer from a familiarity bias—he was eager to explore the unknown world of India at age nineteen. Unfortunately, he got sick and lost a lot of weight. Yet, years later, he credits his experiences in India for giving him confidence to trust his intuition. He made a lot of brilliant choices and some questionable ones thanks to his unique decision-making style, which balanced rationality and intuition.
questions.prompt: What benefit did Jobs later attribute to his Indian experiences?
options: Immunity to illness for the rest of his life.
Confidence to trust his intuition.
A decision style based on rationality alone.
An absence of any questionable decisions.

optionsZh: 终身免疫疾病。
更有信心信任直觉。

从未作可疑决定。
analyses: A 旅行中反而生病且消瘦。
B he credits 是 Jobs 的归因，不是实验确立印度之旅因果。
C balanced rationality and intuition 同时包含两者。
D some questionable ones 明说也有可疑选择。

evidence.quote: he credits his experiences in India for giving him confidence to trust his intuition.

vocabulary.context: 与理性平衡的决策因素，而非保证正确的能力

questions.translation: Steve Jobs 没有受熟悉偏误束缚，十九岁就渴望探索未知的印度。不幸的是，他生病、瘦了很多。但多年后，他把信任直觉的信心归功于印度经历。他独特、平衡理性与直觉的风格，带来许多出色选择，也有一些可疑选择。
questions.editorialStatus: 完整PDF118–122原页视觉核对和跨页拼接。列车118接触/97回收/另105想象者分开，随机分组结果是自报愉快不作长期普适保证。Jobs自我归因与作者传记叙述非实验；海外生活MBA比较不擅加随机性；多文化机制保留speculate/seem、综述不冒充全部因果。DIY及微笑为作者个人文化经验，不推广为全体日本人规范；道德相对主义和作弊保留correlated，不诊断个体。Jobs艺术引语不当实证，奖励保留might。第11章逆境先设问，Nietzsche地震是哲学隐喻并承认破坏，非受害者必然成长或医学处方。不宣称逐句直接证据全覆盖。

questions.passage: Steve Jobs was idiosyncratic, a true one and only. Is there anything generalizable from his experience in India? Or is it specific only to him? Social psychologists Angela Ka-yee Leung, William Maddux, Adam Galinsky, and Chi-yue Chiu have amassed evidence showing that multicultural experiences seem to increase creativity.
questions.prompt: Why ask whether anything from Jobs’s experience is generalizable?
options: To prove a single biography represents everyone.
To reject all research on creativity.
To claim India was the only multicultural setting studied.
To move from an unusual individual toward broader evidence.
questions.promptZh: 为何追问 Jobs 经历能否推广？
optionsZh: 证明一人生平代表所有人。
拒绝全部创造力研究。
称印度是唯一所研究多文化场景。
从独特个人转向更广泛证据。
analyses: A idiosyncratic/one and only 正提出推广疑问。
B 后面引入研究证据。
C 没限定唯一国家。
D 从 specific only to him 到 amassed evidence 构成论述桥梁；seem 需保留，不能单一传记直接推广。

evidence.quote: Is there anything generalizable from his experience in India?
multicultural experiences seem to increase creativity.

vocabulary.context: 能否超出一个独特人物，适用于更广范围
vocabulary.example: A single case may not be generalizable.

questions.translation: Steve Jobs 独特，真正独一无二。他印度经历有什么可推广之处吗？还是只适用于他？社会心理学家 Angela Ka-yee Leung、William Maddux、Adam Galinsky、Chi-yue Chiu 已积累证据，显示多文化经历似乎增加创造力。
